E3 addresses SRO in a different alloy (CoCuFeNiPd) and does not involve cold drawing or Cu-content variation, so it provides no direct support for the key premises. The hypothesis relies on E1 for most claims, but the cited evidence is incomplete and partly mismatched.
premises: Increasing Cu content in Co–Cu–Fe–Mn–Ni promotes spinodal-like phase separation during heavy cold drawing.
This phase separation produces a refined dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The lamellar microstructure contains abundant deformation-induced nano-twins.
Nano-twins enhance toughness by crack deflection and displacement accommodation.
The Cu-modified alloy will show higher toughness than a lower-Cu baseline under identical processing.
